title: Brainstorm x3w: Ask clarifying questions
description: Ask focused questions one at a time to clarify scope, constraints, and success criteria for multiple rules-pack support.
notes:
Clarification: support both concepts: (1) mutually distinct base RPG systems such as D&D vs Pathfinder, and (2) additive/expansion rules packs that layer onto a compatible base system. Campaign binding should distinguish base system identity from ordered compatible add-ons rather than treating all active packs as equivalent.
Clarification: additive rules packs must have explicit load order/precedence. The campaign binding should persist an ordered add-on list, not an unordered set, so lookup and validation can make deterministic conflict decisions.
Clarification: same-key conflicts across ordered rules packs must be explicit. A later add-on may override a base/add-on record only when the record or pack declares an explicit override relationship; accidental duplicate keys fail validation.
Clarification: module/adventure packs must declare rules requirements: required base rules system plus any required/compatible add-on packs. Campaign creation should reject a module paired with an incompatible rules binding before forking campaign content.
Clarification: the first non-D&D sample/fixture should be based on a real open-licensed RPG system, not an invented toy-only rules model. Candidate selection must be verified against primary license/source materials before bundling or test fixture inclusion.
Clarification: the first real non-D&D fixture should be Pathfinder, preferably Pathfinder 2e Remaster/ORC-licensed material unless later requirements select a different Pathfinder edition/source.
Clarification: include rules-system-aware character generation in the first implementation plan. Pathfinder coverage should extend beyond pack loading/lookup into character creation validation, while preserving existing D&D SRD character creation behavior.
Clarification: Pathfinder character generation should be broad/playable rather than a narrow level-1 test-only subset. The implementation plan should still stage this carefully because Pathfinder character creation spans ancestry, background, class, ability boosts, proficiencies, feats, equipment, spells, and validation interactions.
Clarification: favor level-1 Pathfinder character generation for the first deliverable, but design data structures and validation seams to allow future level advancement without replacing the rules-pack model.
close_reason: Clarified base vs add-on packs, explicit order and overrides, module compatibility, Pathfinder fixture, and broad level-1 character generation scope.
